US central bank cuts rates again as jobs market cools

Published 2026-10-07 19:15 UTC

The US central bank has cut interest rates for the third time this year as it tries to shore up a weakening jobs market. The Federal Reserve lowered its key rate by 0.25 percentage points to a range of between 3.25% and 3.5%.

In a statement, the Fed said job gains had slowed and the risks to employment had increased, though inflation remained somewhat elevated. Two officials on the rate-setting committee voted to hold rates.

Fed chair Jerome Powell said further cuts were not guaranteed and would depend on the data. The decision lowers borrowing costs for American households and businesses, and US shares rose after the announcement.
